title: How do you accurately verify a business’s industry, NAICS, or MCC code for underwriting?
summary: Learn how commercial lenders accurately verify small business industry classifications, NAICS codes, and MCC codes to enforce credit policies and avoid prohibited industries.
body_markdown:
### What is the difference between NAICS, SIC, and MCC codes?


[NAICS](https://www.census.gov/naics/) is the federal classification standard used by statistical agencies to classify business establishments by economic activity. Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) is an older system that NAICS largely replaced for federal reporting, though some commercial databases still use it. Merchant Category Codes (MCCs) are four-digit numbers used in payment card networks to classify a merchant’s type of business for transaction processing.


### Why do businesses misclassify their NAICS or MCC codes?


A business may pick an incorrect code because the list is confusing, because operations evolved, or because the applicant sought to bypass an underwriting rule or qualify for a different rate. Investigate differences between sources rather than assuming every misclassification is deliberate fraud.


### Can lenders use website crawling to verify an applicant's business activity?


Yes, as one input among others. Automated tools can scan public website text, service descriptions, and customer terms to see whether the visible business matches the application. Compare the findings with registration, tax, or payment records before drawing conclusions.


### What should a lender do when sources show different industry codes?


Compare the dates and scope of each source. A state formation filing may reflect past plans, a tax return reflects a past year, and a website shows current offerings. Route unresolved differences to an underwriter to confirm what the company currently does before applying policy rules.
